prompt: Build the binary string of a non-negative int by hand with a loop of % 2 and / 2 -- calling Integer.toBinaryString is not allowed.
explanation: Repeatedly taking n % 2 peels off the lowest binary digit and n / 2 shifts the rest of the number down, so the loop produces the digits from last to first. Collecting them in a StringBuilder and calling reverse() at the end puts them in the right order. Zero needs a special case because the loop body never runs when n is already 0.
hints: Handle n == 0 first by returning "0" -- the loop below will not produce anything for it.
While n > 0: append n % 2 to a StringBuilder, then set n = n / 2.
The digits come out backwards; StringBuilder.reverse() fixes the order in one call.
